issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: You need to add a quart of oil every week or two, the oil level is low at every check, and there may be blue smoke at startup. Run too low, the engine can knock or seize, often with no oil light warning first.
issues.why: The piston rings on this 2.4L engine don't seal well and let oil burn in the cylinders. Toyota acknowledged it with a warranty program (ZE7) that covered 2007-2010 tC models, but that coverage has now expired.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every fill-up and keep a quart in the trunk. Ask a shop for an oil consumption test. Many owners live with it by topping up; the real fix is new pistons and rings or a replacement engine.

issues.t: Moonroof glass shatters while driving
issues.sym: A loud bang while driving, often at highway speed, followed by broken glass falling into the cabin or onto the car. Many owners say nothing hit the glass.
issues.why: Owners have filed dozens of NHTSA complaints about the large tC moonroof glass suddenly breaking, sometimes on low-mileage cars. No single cause has been confirmed.
issues.next: If it shatters, pull over safely and cover the opening. Check whether your car has open recalls and file an NHTSA complaint. A glass shop or dealer can replace the panel; check whether your insurance glass coverage applies.

issues.t: Head bolt threads strip, causing coolant leaks
issues.sym: Coolant slowly disappears, the engine runs hot, or coolant seeps from where the cylinder head meets the engine block. It can look like a failed head gasket.
issues.why: On these engines the threads in the block for the cylinder head bolts can pull out, so the head loses clamping force and coolant leaks. Toyota issued a bulletin (S-SB-0004-11) for all 2005-2006 and some 2007 tC models.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and temperature gauge and stop if it overheats. A shop should check the head bolts when doing any head gasket work; the fix is installing threaded steel inserts in the block.

issues.t: Water pump leaking coolant
issues.sym: Pink or green coolant drips under the front of the engine, a sweet smell, a falling coolant level, or a whining noise from the engine belt area.
issues.why: The water pump seal on this engine can wear out and start leaking, often somewhere around 55,000-65,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and look for drips. Replace the pump before it fails completely and the engine overheats.

issues.t: Check engine light from faulty VVT-i oil control valve
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with a rough idle or less power. Codes often point to camshaft timing.
issues.why: The variable valve timing system uses an oil-controlled valve and gear. A sticking valve, often from sludgy or low oil, sets the light. Low oil from the oil-burning problem makes it worse.
issues.next: Have the codes read and check the oil level first. Often the oil control valve or its screen needs cleaning or replacing.

issues.t: Side and curtain airbags may not inflate fully (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. In a crash the side, curtain or knee airbags may not fill properly.
issues.why: Some airbag inflators were built with too little of the chemical that heats the gas, so the bags might not inflate as designed.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN. Dealers replace the affected airbags for free.

issues.t: Side airbags can go off when a door is slammed (recall)
issues.sym: The side seat and curtain airbags suddenly deploy when a door is shut hard with the key on, or shortly after turning the car off.
issues.why: The side impact sensors could read a hard door slam as a crash.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN. Dealers replace both side sensors and add door padding if needed, for free.

issues.t: Moonroof wind deflector glass can shatter (recall)
issues.sym: If road debris hits the tilted-up glass wind deflector at highway speed, the glass can break and pieces can fly off.
issues.why: The glass wind deflector on the moonroof could shatter and separate from its frame when struck.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN. Dealers add a protective film so broken glass stays together.

issues.t: Manual transmission grinds or shifts roughly
issues.sym: Grinding when shifting gears, especially into second or third, or notchy, hard shifts.
issues.why: Owners report worn clutch parts or worn synchronizers (the parts that match gear speeds) in the 5-speed manual.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid and have the clutch adjustment checked. If grinding continues, a shop can tell whether the clutch or the transmission synchronizers are at fault.

issues.t: Rear hatch handle or latch panel breaks
issues.sym: The outside hatch handle snaps off, or the hatch won't open even though the doors unlock.
issues.why: The plastic handle and latch trim on the rear hatch can crack with normal use.
issues.next: Replace the handle or latch trim. In the meantime the hatch can usually be released from inside with the trim removed.

issues.t: Missing load capacity label (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom you can feel. The tire and loading sticker on the door jamb is missing.
issues.why: Some cars were sold without the required label showing how much weight the car can carry, which could lead to overloading.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN. A correct label is mailed or installed for free.

issues.t: A/C not cooling properly
issues.sym: The A/C blows cool instead of cold, or warms up after a while, and may need recharging again soon after a repair.
issues.why: Refrigerant leaks and worn A/C parts are the usual cause. Toyota has issued bulletins telling technicians to find the root cause of leaks because repeat repairs were common.
issues.next: Have the system checked with a leak detector rather than just recharged. Fixing the leak first saves paying for repeated recharges.

issues.t: Moonroof rattles or wind noise
issues.sym: Rattling from the moonroof over bumps, or loud wind noise with the moonroof open at around 45 mph and above.
issues.why: Loose moonroof parts can rattle, and Toyota issued a bulletin (S-SB-0035-12) for wind noise with the moonroof fully open.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to adjust the moonroof and check the bulletin. Opening the roof part way usually reduces the wind noise.

issues.t: Growl or rattle when releasing the clutch
issues.sym: A growling or rattling noise from the transmission area when you let the clutch pedal out, most noticeable at idle.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin (S-SB-0008-13) for this noise on manual-transmission cars. Owners report worn release bearings or internal transmission noise.
issues.next: Have a shop check whether the noise changes with the clutch pedal pressed. If it gets louder or the clutch slips, plan for a clutch and release bearing job.

issues.t: Brief rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A loud knock or rattle from the engine for about one second right after starting a cold engine.
issues.why: The variable valve timing gear on the intake camshaft can rattle before oil pressure builds. Toyota issued a bulletin (S-SB-0010-13) for 2011-2012 tC models built before a production change.
issues.next: It isn't usually harmful right away, but have a dealer check the bulletin. Use the correct 0W-20 oil and keep it changed on time.

issues.t: Check engine light with crankshaft sensor code P0335
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0335; in some cases the engine may stall or be hard to start.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin (SSB-0025-12) for this code and improved the intake camshaft gear assembly. A failing crankshaft position sensor can cause the same code.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer about the bulletin before replacing parts.

issues.t: TRD brake kit hoses can fail (recall)
issues.sym: If your car has the optional TRD big brake kit, the brake pedal can feel soft or the car may take longer to stop.
issues.why: The brake hoses in some TRD brake kits sold as accessories could wear out over time and leak.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check the recall with your VIN. If the kit is installed, Toyota swaps it for a standard brake setup for free.

issues.t: Water on the passenger floor from a clogged A/C drain
issues.sym: Wet carpet or water dripping on the passenger side floor, often after using the A/C, and sometimes a musty smell.
issues.why: The A/C drain tube can clog with debris or even insect nests, so condensation backs up into the cabin. Toyota has several bulletins on this.
issues.next: Have the A/C drain tube cleared and the carpet dried to prevent mold. It is a quick fix.

issues.t: Seat back loose or rattling
issues.sym: The driver's seat back feels loose, rocks or rattles, and in some reports the seat feels like it is coming loose from the car.
issues.why: Owners report loose seat hardware and recliner parts on these years.
issues.next: Have the seat mounting bolts and recliner checked right away; a loose seat is a safety issue in a crash.

issues.t: Door lock actuator failure
issues.sym: A door won't lock or unlock with the remote or switch, or makes a buzzing sound.
issues.why: The small electric motor inside the door latch wears out.
issues.next: Replace the door lock actuator. Lock that door by hand until it is fixed.

issues.t: Paint chipping easily
issues.sym: Chips appear quickly on the hood and front end, even on a low-mileage car.
issues.why: Owners report the paint chips more easily than expected from normal road debris.
issues.next: Touch up chips quickly to stop rust, and consider clear paint protection film on the front.

issues.t: Bluetooth drops or texts don't show on screen
issues.sym: The phone disconnects from Bluetooth, won't reconnect, or iPhone text messages don't appear on the display.
issues.why: Owners report Bluetooth connection trouble, and Toyota issued a tech tip (S-TT-0094-15) about iPhone messages not showing.
issues.next: Delete and re-pair the phone, update the phone software, and ask the dealer about head unit updates.

issues.t: Load label doesn't count installed accessories (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom you can feel. The loading sticker on the door jamb may list too high a carrying capacity.
issues.why: The label didn't account for the weight of accessories installed before sale.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN. A corrected label is provided for free.
